text:
morgan: Quick flag — sample-edge TS types are regressing after our esbuild step. Generic payloads lose inference and become `any`. Repro in samples/edge-ts. Anyone seen bundler/type drift like this?

lee: I ran into this with a different SDK. Usually it's because the published .d.ts and the runtime bundle diverge. Are we publishing both ESM and CJS .d.ts or only one?

morgan: We publish a single types entrypoint in package.json pointing at `dist/index.d.ts`. The edge sample builds everything into one bundle so tsc picks up node resolution while devs use esbuild-style resolution.

toni: Can you paste the smallest repro? Overload mistakes are common cause.

morgan: Sure:

```ts
// app code
const client = new Client();
const out = await client.fetchTyped<{ name: string }>( { model: 'rwd-lite', prompt: 'hi' } );
// after build, out is any
```

and types look like:

```ts
fetchTyped<T>(opts: FetchOpts & { format: 'json' }): Promise<T>
fetchTyped(opts: FetchOpts): Promise<any>
```

I think the second fallback is widening inference.

lee: Right. If TS can't choose the first overload reliably across module boundaries it picks the broader one. Two approaches: make the fallback generic `fetchTyped<T = any>(opts: FetchOpts): Promise<T>` so inference preserves T, or return `Promise<unknown>` for the fallback.

toni: I prefer `unknown` over `any` in public types. It forces callers to narrow and avoids accidental leaks. But this will break some call sites; we should ship a migration note.

morgan: Also spotted `skipLibCheck: true` in the sample tsconfig which masks other mismatches. CI used to run with skipLibCheck true for speed but that's hiding these subtle problems.

ci-bot: CI types job failed: samples/edge-ts/src/main.ts:15 "Type 'any' is not assignable to type '{ name: string }'". Job: https://ci.internal/6789

lee: Another gotcha is module resolution mode. For esbuild/edge we should set `moduleResolution: 'bundler'` and `module: 'ESNext'`. Node samples should use `module: 'NodeNext'`/`moduleResolution: 'nodenext'` if consumers use node ESM. Mismatch in moduleResolution can cause different .d.ts to be selected.

toni: Agreed. Also check `esModuleInterop` and `allowSyntheticDefaultImports`. Those flip import shapes which sometimes change inference if types use `export =` vs `export default`.

morgan: Plan: 1) change fallback overload to `Promise<unknown>` + add narrow helper (e.g., `asJson<T>(v): T`), 2) add a tsd test asserting `fetchTyped<{ name: string }>` infers correctly, 3) update samples/edge-ts/tsconfig.json to `moduleResolution: 'bundler'` and disable `skipLibCheck` in CI.

lee: Please add a small doc in samples/README.md explaining recommended tsconfig per target runtime (edge vs node). Saves future pain.

dev-bot: created issue #432: "edge sample types: overload inference + tsconfig mismatch" assigned to morgan.

morgan: Thanks — I'll open a PR with the type change + tsd test. Will add changelog note if fallback visibility changes.

toni: One more thing: add a dtsnapshot test that validates our published `dist/index.d.ts` contains the expected overloads; helps catch packaging issues when rollups flatten types.

ci-bot: rerun: types job passed after temporary pin to older SDK types (jobs/6789).

morgan: good to know. I'll avoid breaking changes and include migration docs. Cheers :smile:
